components.note: 手 (hand) — in the traditional form 擊, 手 contributed the meaning of striking with force, the source of 击's meaning 'to hit, strike.'
攵 (a striking hand) — 败 relates to being struck down or defeated.
贝 (bèi) gives a sound close to bài, sharing the same initial.
车 (cart) — relates to 转's meaning 'to turn, change direction,' like a wheel turning.
专 (zhuān) gives a sound hint — 转 is pronounced zhuǎn, sharing the same base sound with a different tone.
身 depicts a person's torso, originally showing a pregnant woman's body — later broadened to mean 'the body' in general.
纟 (thread) — 统 relates to threads gathered into one continuous strand, extending to the idea of unifying or governing as one system.
充 (chōng) gives a hint of the sound — 统 is pronounced tǒng, a connection that has shifted somewhat.
氵 (water) — 治 relates to managing or controlling the flow of water, such as flood control.
台 (a platform, structure) — a structure used to direct and control water gave 治 its meaning 'to govern' or 'to manage.'
辶 (to walk) — 遭 relates to something you come across or run into on your way.
曹 (cáo) gives a sound distantly related to zāo, having drifted apart over time.
辶 (to walk) — encountering someone often happens while moving or traveling.
禺 (yú) gives a sound close to yù, with the tone shifted.
纟 (thread) — relates directly to 线's meaning 'line, thread, wire.'
戋 (jiān) served as the phonetic base; its pronunciation has since drifted well away from xiàn.
电 (simplified from 電) depicts a bolt of lightning — since lightning is a natural form of electricity, the character came to mean 'electricity.'
又 (a hand) — reaching to take hold of something.
耳 (ear) — from an ancient battlefield practice of taking a fallen enemy's ear as proof of a kill, the origin of 取's meaning 'to take, obtain.'
氵 (water) — the sea or river being traveled through
斿 — a banner streaming in the wind, evoking free, drifting movement
彳 depicts a step with the left foot; together with 亍 (a step with the right foot), 行 shows a person walking or moving.
亍 depicts a step with the right foot, complementing 彳 to form the idea of walking or travel.
⺼ (flesh) — 胡 originally referred to the flesh under an animal's chin or throat
古 (gǔ) gives the sound — an exact match with 胡's reading hú
讠 (speech radical) — shows 说 relates to talking or language
兑 (duì) is the phonetic component; historically 说 was also pronounced closer to 兑's sound before shifting to shuō
Two lines curving apart from each other, originally meaning 'to divide, split' — the shape was later adopted to represent the number 'eight.'
辶 (to walk) — 道 relates to a path or road one walks along.
首 (shǒu) is the historical phonetic element; its modern reading no longer resembles dào, a reminder that sound components can drift after thousands of years of pronunciation change.
开 (open, here representing a frame or opening) — 形 pictures light passing through a gap.
彡 (streaks or rays of light) — light and pattern coming through an opening gave 形 its meaning 'shape' or 'form.'
弋 (an awl or tool) — one of the craftsman's instruments.
工 (a measuring square) — a tool for making things to a fixed pattern, giving 式 its meaning 'style, form, type.'
口 (mouth) — 嘴 refers directly to the mouth, or a beak-like spout.
觜 (zī) gives a sound distantly related to zuǐ, having drifted apart over time.
Mouth — lips surround the mouth.
Gives the sound chén, related to chún but drifted apart over time.
矛 is a simplified picture of a long spear, its point aimed up and to the right.
厂 depicts a slanted overhang, here standing for a protective shield.
目 (eye) — an eye peering out from behind the shield 厂 gives 盾 its meaning 'shield.'
王 (a variant of 玉, meaning jade) — a valuable object one might glimpse or notice.
见 (to see) — catching sight of something links to the meanings 'to appear, present, now.'
豕 (pig/boar) — appears as part of 象's original full-body pictograph of an elephant, reusing a four-legged-animal shape; 象 itself depicts an elephant's trunk and ears above the body.
纟 (thread) — 结 relates to tying or knotting threads together.
吉 (jí) gives a hint of the sound — 结 is pronounced jié, a connection that has shifted over time.
A simple line drawing of a person's legs seen from the side, used to depict a human being.
木 (tree) — 相 pictures looking closely at a tree.
目 (eye) — staring closely at a tree to examine it gave 相 the meaning 'to observe' or, later, 'each other, mutual.'
亻 (a person), shown twice — one person next to another, similar in shape, the source of 似's meaning 'to resemble, similar, like.'
夂 (to go) — heading out.
田 (farm field) — going out to the fields ahead of the harvest season, the act of preparation giving 备 its meaning 'to prepare, get ready.'
王 (jade, written without its dot) — 玩 originally meant to handle and admire a piece of jade, extending to 'to play, to have fun.'
元 (yuán) gives a sound distantly related to wán, having drifted apart over time.
亻 (person) — 偶 originally described a wooden figure or idol shaped like a person, later extending to 'a pair' and 'by chance.'
禺 (yú) gives a sound distantly related to 偶's reading ǒu, having drifted apart over time.
页 (head) — relates to 领's meaning 'neck, collar; to lead,' the head/neck area.
令 (lìng) gives a sound hint — 领 is pronounced lǐng, sharing the same rhyme with a different tone.
土 (earth) — 域 names a bounded area of land, a territory.
或 (huò) reflects the character's historical phonetic root; the modern reading yù has since diverged.
辶 (walking/movement) — links 边's meaning to a boundary or edge one moves along.
臱 (biān) gives the sound — 边 is also pronounced biān, an exact match.
纟 (thread) — 缘 originally described the hemmed edge of cloth, extended to mean 'connection, fate.'
彖 (tuàn) gives a sound distantly related to yuán, having drifted apart over time.
大 (big) — in 头's simplified form, this element is linked to the idea of 'high' or topmost, since the head sits at the top of the body.
阝 (a variant of 邑, meaning place/settlement) — 部 relates to a division, section, or department.
咅 supplies the sound for 部 (bù); it belongs to the same phonetic family as related characters like 倍 (bèi) and 培 (péi).
氵 (water) — relates to 清's meaning 'clear (water), pure.'
青 (qīng) gives the sound — 清 is also pronounced qīng, an exact match.
扌 (hand) — 振 describes shaking or waving something with the hand.
辰 (chén) gives a sound distantly related to zhèn, having drifted apart over time.
亻 (person) plus 乍 (suddenly/for the first time) — together suggesting a person making or doing something for the first time.
八 (to divide/split apart) — represents something already split into parts.
刀 (knife) — a knife cutting already-divided pieces further, giving 分 its meaning 'to divide, to separate.'

meanings: (lit. and fig.) to come back to life

components.note: 亻 (a person) — the one repeating the routine.
日 (day, sun) — going somewhere every day, a repeated routine giving 复 its meaning 'to repeat, return; again.'
氵 (water) — 活 relates to water flowing, a symbol of life and vitality.
舌 (shé) gives a hint of the sound — 活 is pronounced huó, a connection that has shifted over time.
又 (hand), doubled — two hands side by side depict a pair, giving 双 its meaning 'pair, both, two.'
⺼ (flesh/body) — 胞 relates to the body, originally the womb.
包 (bāo) is an exact match for the sound of 胞.
⺼ (flesh) — 胎 originally named an unborn child inside the body.
台 (tái) gives the sound — a close match for tāi, differing only in tone.
A single horizontal stroke — the simplest possible way to represent the number one; some traditional interpretations link it to heaven or earth as the very first stroke of creation.
阝 (a mound/formation) — soldiers arranged in position
车 (chariot) — war chariots lined up in formation
A simple drawing of a swaddled baby — arms reaching out, legs bundled together in a wrap.
口 (mouth) — used when asking a question aloud
那 (nà) gives a sound close to 哪's reading nǎ, differing mainly in tone
二 (two) — 些 originally suggested a small plural amount, building on the idea of 'more than one.'
此 (cǐ) is the historical phonetic element; it no longer closely matches the modern reading xiē.
彡 (hair/decorative strokes) — 修 relates to grooming, decorating, or improving something
攸 (yōu) gives a sound close to 修's reading xiū, sharing a similar historical pronunciation
王 (a variant form of 玉, meaning jade) — 理 originally referred to the natural grain or pattern in jade, later extending to 'reason, logic, to manage.'
里 (lǐ) gives the sound — 理 is also pronounced lǐ, an exact match.
⺼ (flesh) — resemblance here is tied to physical, bodily likeness.
⺌ (a form related to 小, 'small') gives the sound — a close match for xiào, differing only in tone.
心 (heart) — 恩 relates to feelings of gratitude and kindness.
因 (yīn) gives the sound — an exact match with 恩.
牛 (ox) — 特 originally referred to a male ox singled out for sacrifice, a special animal set apart from the herd.
寺 (sì) gives a hint of the sound — 特 is pronounced tè, a connection that has drifted over time.
力 (strength) — 勒 relates to tightening or restraining with force.
革 (gé) reflects the character's historical phonetic root, though the modern reading lēi has diverged considerably.
夭 (a person leaning back) — the pose of someone laughing.
⺮ (bamboo-like strokes) — suggesting a wide grin, giving 笑 its meaning 'to laugh, smile.'
宀 (roof/house) — 容's meaning 'to contain, hold' relates to a house holding things, extended to 'appearance, to allow, tolerate.'
扌 (hand) — relates to 据's meaning 'to rely on, according to,' as if grasping evidence in hand.
居 (jū) gave the base sound; the pronunciation later shifted to jù, keeping the same final but a different tone.
讠 (speech radical) — shows 说 relates to talking or language
兑 (duì) is the phonetic component; historically 说 was also pronounced closer to 兑's sound before shifting to shuō
电 (simplified from 電) depicts a bolt of lightning — since lightning is a natural form of electricity, the character came to mean 'electricity.'
氵 (water) shows 池 relates to a body of water.
也 (yě) gives a sound distantly related to chí, having drifted apart over time.
户 (door) — 居 relates to where one lives, behind a door
古 (gǔ) gives a sound related to 居's reading jū, from an older, closer pronunciation link
巳 (here representing an eye) — in one traditional theory, this depicted a captive's marked eye, an ancient sign of subjugation, which later broadened to mean 'the common people.'
戈 (a dagger-axe) — combined with the eye shape above, this ties the character to the idea of marking or piercing.
平 depicts a balance scale drawn level and symmetrical — a simple picture of flatness and equality.
宀 (a roof, house) — 安 pictures shelter.
女 (woman) — a woman safely inside a house gave 安 its meaning 'peace' or 'safety.'
Hand — moving things is done by hand.
Gives the sound bān, matching the character's reading.
土 (here representing a person swinging their arms, not its usual meaning 'earth') — depicts someone in motion.
止 (a foot) — combined with the moving figure above, 走 shows a person walking or running.
虫 (insect) — an older semantic link to beeswax, made by insects.
昔 (xī) gives a sound distantly related to là, having drifted apart over time.
火 (fire) — 烛 relates to a flame.
虫 (chóng) gives a sound distantly related to zhú, having drifted apart over time.
日 (sun) — 星 relates to bright heavenly bodies like the sun and stars
生 (shēng) gives a sound close to 星's reading xīng
月 (moon) — 期 relates to time measured by the moon's cycles, like a period or term.
其 (qí) gives a hint of the sound — 期 is pronounced qī, a connection that has shifted slightly in tone.
木 (tree) — traditionally read as a tree that has borne fruit.
立 (standing) — standing close by to watch it grow, evoking closeness and nurture, extended to 亲's meaning 'close, dear; parent, relative.'
A simple line drawing of a person's legs seen from the side, used to depict a human being.
宀 (roof) — 家 is about a home, the space under a roof.
豕 (shǐ, 'pig') supplies the ancient sound for 家; keeping a pig under one's roof was also a practical sign of a household in ancient China, though the modern readings jiā and shǐ no longer rhyme.
丁 (a stylized handle/hook shape in the ancient form) — part of the character's original picture, now mostly opaque in the modern form
口 (kǒu, mouth) gives a sound related to 可's pronunciation kě, and may connect to 可's sense of approval spoken aloud
上 (top) — the upper edge pressing down
卜 — the lower edge, with a card squeezed between the two
辶 (to walk) — 迅 relates to fast movement.
卂 pictures something darting forward quickly, giving 迅 its meaning 'rapid, fast.'
辶 (to walk/move) — 速 relates to the speed of movement
束 (shù) gives a loose sound connection to 速's reading sù
米 (grain, especially husked rice) — 精's meaning 'refined, essence, spirit' relates to rice refined to its purest form.
青 (qīng) gives a sound hint — 精 is pronounced jīng, sharing the same rhyme though the initial consonant differs.
礻 (an altar, related to ritual/spirits) — 神 relates to gods and spirits.
申 (shēn) gives a hint of the sound — 神 is pronounced shén, a connection that has shifted over time.
疒 (sickness) — relates directly to 病's meaning 'illness, disease, to be sick.'
丙 (bǐng) gives a sound hint — 病 is pronounced bìng, sharing the same base sound with a different tone.
木 (wood) — 棺 names a wooden box used for burial, a coffin.
官 (guān) gives the sound — an exact match with 棺.
木 (wood) — 材 originally named timber.
才 (cái) gives the sound — an exact match with 材.
页 (head) — relates to 领's meaning 'neck, collar; to lead,' the head/neck area.
令 (lìng) gives a sound hint — 领 is pronounced lǐng, sharing the same rhyme with a different tone.
巾 (cloth) — the bottom half of a belt, hanging straight down.
Above the cloth, the strokes crease as if folded at the waist — depicting a belt or sash, the source of 带's meaning 'belt, band,' later 'to bring, carry along.'
The character traces the front view of an ox's head, with the top stroke and crossing lines representing its curved horns and ears.
扌 (hand) — 排 relates to arranging things by hand into order
非 (fēi) gives a sound distantly related to 排's reading pái, having drifted apart over time
忄 (heart) — 情 relates to feelings and emotions.
青 (qīng) gives the sound — 情 is pronounced qíng, a close match differing only in tone.
开 (open, here representing a frame or opening) — 形 pictures light passing through a gap.
彡 (streaks or rays of light) — light and pattern coming through an opening gave 形 its meaning 'shape' or 'form.'
羊 (sheep) — work involving livestock, done imperfectly
工 (work) — the labor itself, linked to the idea of falling short
力 (strength) — 劲 names physical strength or energy.
辶 (to walk) — 途 names a road or path traveled on.
余 (yú) gives a sound distantly related to tú, having drifted apart over time.
辶 (walking/movement) — links 边's meaning to a boundary or edge one moves along.
臱 (biān) gives the sound — 边 is also pronounced biān, an exact match.
A short stroke placed above a longer one — a simple graphic way to show 'up' or 'above,' contrasted with 下 (down), which flips the strokes.
